biggestGap: The central test still fails on its own numbers: at +50 ms the fast flick's free droplets are median 4.0 px and 76.3% juice-tinted while the slow cleave's are median 3.0 px and 77.6% juice-tinted — fast is neither finer NOR less saturated than slow, because one speed-independent class (84 cling beads, juice-tinted, ~13 px each) owns 68% of the fast frame's particle pixels and drags it back to the slow frame's statistics.
method_note: The r2 verdict did not ship its probe script. I rebuilt it (lum>0.06, 8-connectivity, components excluded if bbox width >0.35*frame or area >1500 px, so the fruit+blade streak merge is dropped) and ran the SAME script over BOTH r2b and r3, so every pair below is a like-for-like delta. My absolute r2b numbers sit a little above the predecessor's (fast median 37.5 px where they reported 26.5) because their threshold was higher; direction and magnitude of the r2b->r3 change are stable across thr 0.06/0.08/0.10/0.12/0.15/0.20 and 4- vs 8-connectivity, so the deltas are real and not a change of method.

why_the_fast_frame_still_reads_tinted.measurement: In r3 15-fast-flick, blobs >=16 px are only 32 of 152 components but carry 1107 of 1623 particle pixels (68% of the pixel mass) at meanSat 0.845. The 67 tiny 1-3 px blobs — the class that is now correctly white at meanSat 0.323 — carry 132 px, 8% of the mass. The white aerosol is right; it is simply outvoted.
why_the_fast_frame_still_reads_tinted.source_traced: /home/claude/juice/src/juice/fluid.js line 1185: `const nCling = Math.round(q.cling * amtK * bk)` — 84 beads at tier 3, with NO `fast` or `filmness` term on the COUNT, and line 1198 `cls(sz * 1.5)` which multiplies the size up through `small = 0.022*szScale` (line 1075) so they are classified juice-coloured. Every other class was correctly gated: nRim is `(0.05 + 1.05*filmness)`, nSpr is `(0.95 - 0.80*fast)*(0.35 + 0.65*heavy)`, nStr is `filmness`. Cling is the one that was missed, and 84 beads x ~13 px = ~1100 px matches the measured 1107 px exactly. It is the cloud of fat orange beads falling to the lower-left of the orange in 15-fast-flick+50ms.

sheet_timeline_still_runs_backwards.conclusion: Amplitude halved but the SHAPE is unchanged — still monotonically increasing to a peak at +500 ms. The bar wants full extent by 30-40 ms and gone by ~130 ms. At +250 ms, 120 ms after the juice should have died, the frame is at 62% of its eventual maximum and still climbing. The only improvement is the tail: +1000 ms went 2490 -> 207 px, so it now clears. Death by tearing is visible at +100 ms; death by the right TIME is not.

evidence.blind_test: Instant, and not a close call. 04-cut+250ms and 00-hero.png are a forest of identical pale-pink spindle billboards — the same asset rotated and repeated dozens of times with straight, hard, mirrored edges — interleaved with perfectly elliptical red beads each carrying one identical white specular dot at the same relative position on every bead. You can count them. plate-02's aerosol is a continuum whose individual grains have no repeated silhouette and no two of which catch the light the same way. 15-fast-flick+50ms is the one frame that hesitates for a moment — the silver arc hugging the cut plane above the orange is close to plate-02's wedge — but the fat orange bead fall beneath it gives it away in under a second.
evidence.combo_check: 09-combo+50ms went median 23.0 px / 4051 particle px (r2b) to 3.0 px / 1393 px (r3), same direction as the central pair — so the size fix is global, not tuned to the test frames.

fix: One change, /home/claude/juice/src/juice/fluid.js line 1185, is worth more than everything else: `const nCling = Math.round(q.cling * amtK * bk)` is the last class with no stroke-speed gate, and by pixel mass it is 68% of the fast flick. Make it `Math.round(q.cling * amtK * (0.12 + 0.88 * filmness) * bk)` and change line 1198's `cls(sz * 1.5)` to `cls(sz * 0.8)` so an atomised citrus face carries the white sheen of tiny bubbles the comment on line 1184 already promises instead of a pink foam. Predicted, and directly measurable on the next 15-vs-16 pair with the probe described in method_note: fast median blob area drops to ~2 px, frac>=16px drops from 21.1% to under 6%, and sat>=0.45 drops from 76.3% to under 30% while the slow cleave holds at ~78% — which is the first time the two frames would differ in kind. Second, and only after that: the envelope at line 1064 (`A.fB.array[i4+3] = (0.078 + 0.050*filmness) * ...`) still yields a particle-pixel budget peaking at +500 ms; the sheet needs to reach full extent inside the first emit and be at <20% of peak by +130 ms, so the lifetime constant is roughly 4x too long and the emission needs to be front-loaded rather than trickled.
